result.title: Concept Generalization in Visual Brain Decoding via Encoder-Generated fMRI
result.summary: Visual brain decoders are typically trained and evaluated on stimuli drawn from similar semantic distributions, leaving their ability to reconstruct unseen concepts poorly understood. We study this concept generalization problem by withholding semantic concepts from a target subject's training data. We find that three recent fMRI-to-image decoders degrade substantially for the held-out concepts, even when the concept remains available for multi-subject models. In contrast, brain encoders that map a pretrained visual representation directly to voxels are markedly more robust to the same semantic holdout. Motivated by this asymmetry, we use such an encoder to generate synthetic fMRI responses for new images and add the resulting image-fMRI pairs to decoder training. Across three decoders, four subjects, and twelve semantic concepts, synthetic data recovers a substantial fraction of the performance lost on unseen concepts without requiring additional, time-consuming fMRI acquisition. We further show that the same approach improves general decoding performance across a wide range of data budgets. Analyses of encoder training conditions, encoder designs, and synthetic-data controls show that the gains depend on both encoder generalization and the semantic content of the synthetic supervision, rather than merely increasing the amount of training data. Together, our results show that encoder-generated fMRI can transfer semantic generalization to decoders.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究 fMRI-to-image 解码器的概念泛化：在目标被试训练数据中留出若干语义概念后，三个解码器性能大幅下降，而将预训练视觉表示直接映射到体素的脑编码器明显更稳健；作者据此用编码器为新图像合成 fMRI 响应并加入解码器训练，在多个解码器、被试和概念上恢复了相当一部分损失性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「视觉表示较稳健、下游解码器对新概念脆弱」的不对称，以及用冻结视觉表示生成合成监督信号的做法，可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 视觉状态是否保留语义、能否泛化到未见概念，以及合成状态监督的有效来源提供类比线索，需读原文核查。
